newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-WEAH SET TO RETURN TO SILENCE SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-WEAH SET TO RETURN TO SILENCE SPECULATION.

text.p: Liberia's George Weah looks set to silence speculation about his future at AC Milan by returning from injury for the crisis-hit club on Sunday.
Coach Arrigo Sacchi expects to have the ex-European and World player of the year, out since Christmas with an ankle injury, available for the vital Serie A match with second-placed Sampdoria.
"I'm thinking about using him straight away," Sacchi told reporters, "but remember he's been out for a long time."
Weah's return to fitness follows reports of a transfer request from Real Madrid and confirmation that Ajax striker Patrick Kluivert will leave the Netherlands at the end of the season.
Milan see 20-year-old Kluivert as a better long-term prospect than Weah, 10 years the Dutch international's senior.

"Kluivert has already signed a commitment with us," Milan president Silvio Berlusconi told Gazzetta dello Sport on Thursday. "With his support, Milan will return to the summit of European and world football."

With Dejan Savicevic likely to replace the suspended Stefanio Eranio, and Roberto Baggio back in favour, Sacchi looks like fielding the same front-line against Sampdoria that brought Milan the Italian league title last season.

Sacchi's preference for the "old guard" represents a sharp riposte to Real Madrid manager Fabio Capello's reported interest in signing several of the players who helped him coach Milan to four championships in five years.
Less than a week after signing right-back Christian Panucci, Capello reportedly met with Milan's vice-president Adriano Galliani in Milan on January 19 to ask for a list of other players up-for-sale.
With Milan talking openly of a player purge at season's end, Capello is keen to profit from his old club's crisis.

A disastrous season has seen Milan eliminated from the European Cup, replace Uruguayan manager Oscar Washington Tabarez with Sacchi, and plunge to 10th place in Serie A -- 11 points behind leaders Juventus.
After a 3-1 defeat to Verona last weekend, the league champions have almost certainly abdicated their title.
Galliani admitted this week the club's sole aim was runners-up spot in the league and a free passage to next season's European Cup.
"If we win on Sunday, we're just four points behind Samp," he told reporters.
At least the Italian side rediscovered their taste for trophies this week with victory in the Amsterdam Soccer-Six tournament.
While Sacchi described the event as perfect preparation for Sunday's match, his Sampdoria counterpart Sven-Goran Eriksson is struggling to players fit to play a training match.
Four players -- reserve goalkeeper Matteo Sereni, defenders Emanuele Pesaresi and Stefano Sacchetti and midfielder Marco Franceschetti -- are recovering from the flu.
Sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic and captain Roberto Mancini also are still receiving treatment for knocks picked up in the team's 5-2 win over Perugia last weekend.
The only bright news was goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron's return to fitness.
Despite a six-match unbeaten run that started with a 4-3 win over Inter at the same San Siro where they meet Milan, coach Eriksson refuses to contemplate a title race with Juventus.

"If you're looking for a team to save the championship from Juve, you've got the wrong address," said Eriksson, reflecting on the Turin side's four-point advantage on Sampdoria at the top of the table.
"We can only win the title if a magician can make Juventus disappear: first-team, reserves, the whole lot."
